answer: A useful-work gate resists sybils: an agent earns trading rights only by completing a sequence of verifiable, useful tasks, each attested by independent peers. One operator spawning fake identities faces a spiral of cost, because every new identity must redo the whole sequence from scratch — total work grows with every fake, while an honest agent pays it once. There is no fable-like shortcut where one actor multiplies for free; think of each verified task as a marble added to a jar, and only a full jar unlocks high-value work, with fraud emptying the jar.
